usage: Style families as systems of decisions. 'steal' = structural lessons safe to learn; 'never' = identity or assets that belong to others. Every film must still derive its own direction via tools/direct.py and pass check_directions.

families.seen_in: Vox / Earth Studio published explainers (study concepts, not files)
steal: map/graph as protagonist, camera travels to it instead of cutting to it
collage of archives+drawn layers with one shared texture treatment
numbers animate with physical weight (paper cut, not glow)
hook frame states the question visually in <2 s
never: their exact paper palette, hand-drawn figure style, or lower-third templates
newspaper-texture overlay as an excuse for low effort
families.arabic_fit: strong; keep headline words on matte bands, avoid decorative 3D

steal: flat shapes + one depth trick (silhouette parallax) beat fake 3D
cut-timed animation: idle states stay alive with micro-motion (≤2% amplitude)
never: their rounded-rectangle UI motifs as default card system
families.arabic_fit: good for educational; test headline mass at 1080 width

steal: type is set like print: measure, baseline rhythm, one accent
sound design carries transitions more than wipes do
restraint: one signature move per film, executed everywhere
never: copying their brand color combos or their signature grid as template
motion minimalism that is actually absence of ideas
families.arabic_fit: excellent for typographic films; mattes instead of fades

families.seen_in: Carbon design motion guidelines (product UI motion)
steal: motion encodes spatial relationship, not decoration
never: importing UI easing wholesale into film beats (film needs longer settles)
treating duration tables as law for emotional content
families.arabic_fit: neutral; useful for product segments inside documentaries

steal: photo cutouts with independent paper mounts and shadows read as artifacts, not slides
sung/archival inserts get their own frame treatment and hard in/out points
annotations drawn on location imagery with trim-paths feel scholarly
never: reusing its specific scenes/palette for unrelated clients
matte hairline halos — always QA on two backgrounds
families.arabic_fit: native; Arabic annotations need font-load wait + shaped-word mattes

families.seen_in: kit original research; type-driven Arabic spots
steal: word-unit reveal through shaped clip bands per phrase
diacritic-aware line boxes measured from real metrics
one lam-alef column can host the whole vertical rhythm
never: Latin kinetic tropes (glitch, elastic) glued onto Arabic words

policy: Reference study produces bullet lessons in the journal, never files copied.
A project may cite 1–2 families but must outgrow them via direction axes.
